title: Coordinate boundary bound for a finitely generated monotone upper set
statement:
Let $n\ge1$. Regard $\mathbf N^n$ as the exponent vectors of monomials in $\mathbf Z[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then use coordinatewise order on $\mathbf N^n$, with $|a|=\sum_{j=1}^n a_j$ and $e_j$ the $j$th coordinate vector. Let $A\subseteq\mathbf N^n$ be finite, let $M\ge1$ be an integer with $|a|\le M$ for every $a\in A$, and put
$$U=\bigcup_{a\in A}(a+\mathbf N^n).$$
Assume $u-u_p e_p+u_p e_t\in U$ whenever $u\in U$ and $1\le p<t\le n$. If $1\le k\le n$, $v\in\mathbf N^n$, $v\notin U$ and $v+e_k\in U$, there exists $a\in A$ with
$$a_k=v_k+1>0,\qquad a_t\le v_t\quad(t\ne k),$$
and
$$v_j<M\qquad(k\le j\le n).$$
The assertion includes $A=\varnothing$ and $U=\mathbf N^n$, when no such $v$ exists, and $k=n$, when there are no coordinates later than $k$.

source.place: Agent combinatorial refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997 section 8, Lemma 8.2 and Remarks 8.4, pp.274--275; Original proof Steps 2--3 and 5--6: the one-coordinate boundary witness and transfer to any large later coordinate; used for the whole diagram and its earlier-vertex prefixes. No Stacks tag states this combinatorial result. ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies only the historical parent route; BM paper read online at https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf and absent from repository literature.

proof.text: For natural vectors $x$, the displayed definition of $U$ says $x\in U$ if and only if some $a\in A$ satisfies $a_t\le x_t$ for all $t$: in one direction write $x=a+b$ with $b\in\mathbf N^n$, and in the other take $b_t=x_t-a_t$. Consequently $a\in U$ for every $a\in A$, and $x\in U$, $x\le y$ imply $y\in U$ by using the same generator.

proof.text: Apply this membership criterion to $v+e_k\in U$, obtaining $a\in A$ with $a\le v+e_k$. Thus $a_t\le v_t$ for $t\ne k$ and $a_k\le v_k+1$. If $a_k\le v_k$, then $a\le v$ and the same criterion gives $v\in U$, a contradiction. Since these are integers, $a_k=v_k+1>0$. Also $v_k+1=a_k\le |a|\le M$, because all summands in $|a|$ are nonnegative; hence $v_k<M$.

proof.text: Fix $j>k$ and suppose $v_j\ge M$. Apply the assumed whole-coordinate transfer to $a\in U$ with $p=k$, $t=j$; it gives $b=a-a_k e_k+a_k e_j\in U$. Coordinatewise, $b_k=0\le v_k$, $b_j=a_j+a_k\le |a|\le M\le v_j$ (here $j\ne k$), and $b_t=a_t\le v_t$ for $t\notin\{k,j\}$. Thus $b\le v$ and the upward closure proved in Step 1 gives $v\in U$, contradicting the hypothesis. Therefore $v_j<M$ for every $j>k$. Together with Step 2 this is the required bound for all $j\ge k$, with the same witness $a$.

proof.text: If $A=\varnothing$, then $U=\varnothing$ by its displayed definition, so $v+e_k\in U$ is impossible. If $U=\mathbf N^n$, then $v\notin U$ is impossible. If $k=n$ (in particular when $n=1$), Step 2 already bounds the only coordinate required; Step 3 has no indices. These cases require no choices from an empty set.

lean.statement: theorem monotone_boundary_box {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (A : Set (Fin n →₀ ℕ)) (hA : A.Finite) (M : ℤ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hdegree : ∀ a ∈ A, (↑(∑ j : Fin n, a j) : ℤ) ≤ M) (htransfer : ∀ u ∈ upperClosure A, ∀ p t : Fin n, p < t → u - Finsupp.single p (u p) + Finsupp.single t (u p) ∈ upperClosure A) (k : Fin n) (v : Fin n →₀ ℕ) (hv : v ∉ upperClosure A) (hvk : v + Finsupp.single k 1 ∈ upperClosure A) : ∃ a ∈ A, a k = v k + 1 ∧ 0 < a k ∧ (∀ t : Fin n, t ≠ k → a t ≤ v t) ∧ (∀ j : Fin n, k ≤ j → (v j : ℤ) < M)
